content.value_statement: API clients need consistent auth, caching, validation, and error handling. This skill guides TanStack Query, Axios, JWT interceptors, Zod parsing, and offline behavior.
actual_capabilities: Configures TanStack Query defaults for caching, retries, stale time, and garbage collection.
Shows an Axios client with base URL, timeout, JWT request headers, and 401 refresh handling.
Defines global API error handling with user-facing toast messages for common HTTP statuses.
Uses Zod schemas to validate API responses and derive TypeScript types.
Builds reusable query and mutation hooks for pagination, optimistic updates, offline checks, and request cancellation.
limitations: Focused on React, Next.js, TypeScript, TanStack Query, Axios, and Zod projects.
Assumes an existing authentication store that can provide sessions, refresh tokens, and sign-out behavior.
Provides implementation guidance and examples, not a runnable package or generated backend API.
Does not define project-specific API contracts beyond the sample student and attendance models.

use_cases.title: Create a React API Layer
use_cases.description: Set up shared API clients, query providers, and reusable hooks for a new frontend project.

use_cases.title: Add Authenticated Requests
use_cases.description: Attach JWT tokens, refresh expired sessions, and redirect users when authentication fails.

use_cases.title: Standardize Data Fetching
use_cases.description: Document consistent caching, validation, error handling, pagination, and optimistic update patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Basics
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new API client foundation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up a typed API client for my React app using TanStack Query and Axios. Include caching defaults, retries, and provider setup.

prompt_templates.title: Add JWT Handling
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for authenticated API calls.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add JWT request headers and 401 refresh handling to my Axios API client. Use my existing auth store for session, refresh, and sign-out actions.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Responses
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for safer response parsing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create reusable API hooks that validate responses with Zod schemas, show useful error messages, and return typed data to components.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Complex Flows
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for production data workflows.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design paginated queries, optimistic mutations, offline detection, and cancelable requests for a production React API layer.

output_examples.input: Set up a new API client with TanStack Query and Axios.
output: A shared query client configuration with retry and cache timing decisions.
An Axios client plan with base URL, timeout, and typed request methods.
Provider integration notes for a React or Next.js application.

output_examples.input: Add authenticated API requests with refresh handling.
output: A request interceptor approach for attaching bearer tokens from the auth store.
A 401 handling flow that refreshes tokens when possible.
A sign-out and login redirect path for failed refresh attempts.

output_examples.input: Build hooks for paginated student data and attendance updates.
output: Reusable query hooks for paginated and infinite list data.
Mutation guidance with cache invalidation and optimistic rollback.
Validation and offline behavior notes for resilient UI states.

best_practices: Keep API base URLs configurable and review production values before release.
Validate server responses before trusting data in UI components.
Centralize auth, errors, retries, and cache invalidation to avoid inconsistent request behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not scatter raw Axios calls across components when shared hooks can enforce consistent behavior.
Do not store private secrets in public client environment variables.
Do not skip rollback handling for optimistic mutations that can fail.

faq.question: What frameworks does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets React and Next.js projects that use TypeScript, TanStack Query, Axios, and Zod.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete backend API?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on frontend API client patterns and assumes the backend contract already exists.

faq.question: Can it work without JWT authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. You can omit the interceptor and refresh sections when your API does not require bearer tokens.

faq.question: Does it support response validation?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use Zod schemas to validate API responses and derive TypeScript types.

faq.question: How does it handle failed requests?
faq.answer: It recommends retry defaults, status-specific error messages, toast notifications, and redirect behavior for failed authentication.

faq.question: Is this skill safe to use with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It is documentation guidance for API client implementation and does not include executable helper scripts.
